lines.text: Eight a.m. A message from the research team. Was last night's run really offline? And can we trust the result?
Here is the whole picture. On the connected side, GitLab prepares everything the workflow needs. Once.
It lands in private AWS storage. Every file is fingerprinted. Every container image is locked to its exact identity.
Then the run happens here, on a host with no route to the internet. Only private AWS endpoints can reach it.
So what if a task tries to reach out? There is nowhere to go. The run stops at stage eight, and says FAIL. Loudly. Never silently.
And when you see PASS, all ten checks passed, offline, with evidence. So you can tell the researcher: yes. Here is the proof.
